items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: this is back when I first went to New York, when I joined Lester Young.

ctx.x: But I finally went on to New York, and it was there that I was inspired by other great piano players like Pete

Johnson and Albert Ammons became very influential in my life, and they taught me the boogie-woogie style. And Pete Johnson was a very warm human being. And he and Albert Ammons both. And the fact of the matter is the way I went to New York was I was sent to play with Lester Young, who was my real love. Actually Lester Young was my real love, because I like to play tenor too.
